articles.title: Patch day: a five-minute routine for re-checking tier lists and weakness charts
articles.excerpt: Patch day: a five-minute routine for re-checking tier lists and weakness charts Every balance patch does the same thing to a game wiki: it quietly invalidates part of yesterday's advice, and the part…
articles.body: Patch day: a five-minute routine for re-checking tier lists and weakness charts Every balance patch does the same thing to a game wiki: it quietly invalidates part of yesterday's advice, and the part it breaks is rarely the part anyone checks first. After a few cycles of planning around numbers that had already changed, I settled on a short routine that takes about five minutes and saves a lot of wasted materials. 1. Ask what kind of number moved. Patch notes list dozens of lines. Most of them are wording, bug fixes or quality-of-life changes that do not move a ranking at all. The ones that do are damage values, cooldowns, resource costs, and anything that changes how often an ability can be used. If a note does not touch one of those, the tier list probably still stands. 2.

articles.title: How Phones Become One Game Board in Your Browser
articles.excerpt: I'm Nikita, an entrepreneur from Ukraine. In about a month I built BIGBOARD.GAMES, a site with free games that friends play together in the browser. I launched it on October 5. A few weeks later my po…
articles.body: I'm Nikita, an entrepreneur from Ukraine. In about a month I built BIGBOARD.GAMES , a site with free games that friends play together in the browser. I launched it on October 5. A few weeks later my post on r/SideProject took off, and people loved my games. So far, more than 2,500 people from 90 countries have played more than 10,000 games. I wrote about that first month on my blog. The idea is simple. You put two to four phones or tablets next to each other on a table, and their screens become one board . In air hockey the puck leaves one screen and comes in on the next one, on the same line and at the same speed. A friend in another city can join from their own phone, and a laptop or a TV can join just to show the board to everyone.

articles.title: Creating a Robot Sensor Data Recording and Replay System
articles.excerpt: A robust recording-and-replay system is the backbone of any serious robot learning workflow. Recording lets you build datasets and debug incidents after the fact; replay lets you re-run recorded senso…
articles.body: A robust recording-and-replay system is the backbone of any serious robot learning workflow. Recording lets you build datasets and debug incidents after the fact; replay lets you re-run recorded sensor streams through your perception or control stack without needing the physical robot, which massively speeds up development and debugging. This tutorial covers building both halves as a cohesive system. Why replay matters as much as recording It's easy to treat recording as "just logging," but a good replay system pays for itself quickly: Debugging without hardware : reproduce a bug from last week's session without booking robot time. Regression testing : replay a fixed set of recorded sessions through a new version of your perception pipeline and diff the outputs.

articles.title: Extracting MP3 audio from a video entirely in the browser with ffmpeg.wasm
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: this article was written with AI assistance and reviewed by me. I built the tool used as the example below. Most "video to MP3" websites upload your file to a server, convert it there and…
articles.body: Disclosure: this article was written with AI assistance and reviewed by me. I built the tool used as the example below. Most "video to MP3" websites upload your file to a server, convert it there and send the result back. For a 500 MB phone video that means a long upload, a queue and a copy of your private video on someone else's disk. Since WebAssembly became fast enough, you can do the whole thing locally in the tab. Here is how it works and the pitfalls I hit. The building block: ffmpeg.wasm ffmpeg.wasm is FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. It exposes a small virtual file system (MEMFS) and an exec function that takes the same arguments as the command-line tool.

articles.body: For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 .
